description: OSRD (Open Source Railway Designer) is an open-source web application for railway infrastructure design, capacity analysis, timetabling, train running simulation and short-term path requests. Users edit infrastructure and timetables to build realistic scenarios, simulate train runs, see conflicts in space-time and track occupancy diagrams, view tracks, signals, detectors and operational points on a map, edit rolling stock, and insert new trains into residual capacity; it is designed to simulate prospective infrastructure formats and custom signalling systems. It is hosted by the OpenRail Association with SNCF Réseau among its sponsors, and developed in the open on GitHub. It is location independent and loads any network in its infrastructure format. The code is licensed LGPL-3.0, free, with a public demo at demo.osrd.fr, documentation on osrd.fr and releases up to v1.3.0, and commits continued in September 2026. Caveats: the developers state it is still in active development with user and programming interfaces that are not entirely stable, and the public demo is reset daily and not for production. OSRD supports capacity planning, network flow and disruption or resilience studies of rail networks and digital twin prototyping, and relates to railML and to the EU Register of Infrastructure, both catalogued here.
